balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For The Japan Steel Works, Ltd.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For The Japan Steel Works, Ltd.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For The Japan Steel Works, Ltd.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For The Japan Steel Works, Ltd.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For The Japan Steel Works, Ltd.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For The Japan Steel Works, Ltd.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For The Japan Steel Works, Ltd.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For The Japan Steel Works, Ltd.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For The Japan Steel Works, Ltd.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue
segmentRevenue.content:
JSW reports two segments: Industrial Machinery (plastics/injection-molding machinery plus defense equipment) and Materials & Engineering (nuclear and thermal power forgings, steel plates and specialty materials).

For The Japan Steel Works, Ltd.: Industrial Machinery is ~82% of FY2026 revenue and carries the defense-equipment order book; Materials & Engineering is the smaller, lower-margin forgings business tied to the nuclear-restart and power-plant replacement cycle in Japan. Only FY2025 and FY2026 are shown -- the segment note is absent from earlier years' English filing translations.

What to watch:

  • Industrial Machinery growth driven by defense versus civilian plastics-machinery demand
  • Whether Materials & Engineering's forgings order book tracks Japan's nuclear-restart schedule

machineryProductMix.title: Industrial Machinery product mix
machineryProductMix.content:
Within Industrial Machinery, JSW discloses three product lines: plastics machinery (injection-molding systems), the molding machine business and defense equipment (artillery, ammunition and related systems for Japan's Ministry of Defense).

For The Japan Steel Works, Ltd.: defense revenue grew from ¥32.2bn (FY2025) to ¥46.9bn (FY2026) on Japan's rising defense budget, even as defense orders fell from ¥115.8bn to ¥87.4bn -- orders lead revenue by roughly a year, so the order drop is worth watching into FY2027. Plastics machinery is the cyclical, export-exposed line.

What to watch:

  • Defense order intake versus Japan's multi-year defense-spending plan
  • Plastics/molding machinery orders as a read on global capex and auto/electronics demand

segmentOperatingIncome.title: Segment operating income
segmentOperatingIncome.content:
Operating income by segment, split the same way as segment revenue.

For The Japan Steel Works, Ltd.: Industrial Machinery earns the bulk of group operating income (¥20.0bn of ¥25.3bn total in FY2026) at a mid-single-digit-point-higher margin than Materials & Engineering, so the mix shift toward machinery (and within it, toward defense) is margin-accretive for the group.

What to watch:

  • Materials & Engineering margin recovery as forgings volumes scale
  • Whether Industrial Machinery margin holds as defense (a different cost structure to civilian machinery) grows within it

defenseOrders.title: Defense orders vs defense revenue
defenseOrders.content:
Defense orders received in a period versus the defense revenue recognised in that same period -- JSW's backlog (orders not yet converted to revenue) moves with the gap between the two.

For The Japan Steel Works, Ltd.: defense revenue has been converting faster than new orders arrive (orders fell FY2025->FY2026 while revenue rose), so the backlog that has driven several years of growth is starting to run down; the next order intake print matters more than the trailing revenue trend.

What to watch:

  • Order intake reaccelerating versus Japan's defense budget cycle
  • Backlog coverage (orders / revenue) trending below 1x for more than one period

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For The Japan Steel Works, Ltd.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
